cards.info: What is a data point that differs significantly from other observations called?
cards.backInfo: An outlier is a data point that is significantly higher or lower than the rest of the values.

cards.info: Why is the mean more sensitive to outliers than the median?
cards.backInfo: The mean is sensitive because its calculation incorporates the specific value of every data point in the set.
cards.imageMarkdown: ![A flow chart showing which statistical measures are sensitive or resistant to outliers.](https://img.justsolvely.com/followUpImage/97bd8f31-7097-445a-9fd2-9e5f2900fe94-1786506131010-641.webp)

cards.info: Why is the median considered a resistant measure of center?
cards.backInfo: The median is resistant because it is determined by the middle position of an ordered data set, not extreme values.

cards.info: Which measure of spread is most affected by extreme maximum or minimum values?
cards.backInfo: The range is highly sensitive to outliers because it is calculated using the maximum and minimum values.

cards.info: Why does the Interquartile Range (IQR) remain stable when outliers are present?
cards.backInfo: The IQR is resistant because it measures the spread of the middle 50% of the data ($Q3 - Q1$).
cards.imageMarkdown: ![A flow chart showing which statistical measures are sensitive or resistant to outliers.](https://img.justsolvely.com/followUpImage/97bd8f31-7097-445a-9fd2-9e5f2900fe94-1786506131010-641.webp)

cards.info: How does adding a very large outlier typically affect the mean and median?
cards.backInfo: A large outlier will increase the mean, while the median will likely remain the same.

cards.info: What happens to the mean when a very small outlier is added?
cards.backInfo: Adding a very small outlier will pull the mean downward (decrease it) while the median likely stays the same.

cards.info: What does a significant difference between mean and median often indicate?
cards.backInfo: A large difference between the mean and median is a strong indicator of outliers or skewed data.

cards.info: Does an increase in range always result in an increased IQR?
cards.backInfo: No; it is a mistake to assume the IQR must increase just because an outlier increased the range.

cards.info: In the set {5, 10, 15, 20, 25}, how does replacing 25 with 500 affect the median?
cards.backInfo: The median remains 15 because the middle position in the ordered set does not change.

cards.info: How is an outlier defined in terms of its value relative to other data?
cards.backInfo: An outlier is a data point that is significantly higher or lower than the rest of the observations.

cards.info: Which measure of center is most likely to change if the largest value increases?
cards.backInfo: The mean is most likely to change because it is sensitive to the magnitude of every data point.
cards.imageMarkdown: ![A flow chart showing which statistical measures are sensitive or resistant to outliers.](https://img.justsolvely.com/followUpImage/97bd8f31-7097-445a-9fd2-9e5f2900fe94-1786506131010-641.webp)

cards.info: Why does changing the largest value to an even larger number not affect the median?
cards.backInfo: The median is resistant because it depends on the middle position, which remains unchanged by extreme values.

cards.info: Why is the range considered an extremely sensitive measure of spread?
cards.backInfo: The range is sensitive because it is calculated solely from the maximum and minimum values, which include outliers.

cards.info: Which measure of spread ignores extreme ends to remain resistant to outliers?
cards.backInfo: The Interquartile Range (IQR) is resistant because it only measures the spread of the middle 50% of data.
cards.imageMarkdown: ![A flow chart showing which statistical measures are sensitive or resistant to outliers.](https://img.justsolvely.com/followUpImage/97bd8f31-7097-445a-9fd2-9e5f2900fe94-1786506131010-641.webp)

cards.info: If a data set's mean increases while the median stays constant, what likely happened?
cards.backInfo: A very large outlier was likely added to or increased within the data set.

cards.info: What is the effect on the mean if a value much lower than the rest is added?
cards.backInfo: The mean will decrease because it is pulled downward by the small outlier.

cards.info: How do you calculate the impact of a new outlier on the range?
cards.backInfo: Subtract the new minimum from the new maximum and compare this result to the original range.

cards.info: What should you suspect if the mean is much higher than the median?
cards.backInfo: You should suspect the presence of high outliers or that the data is skewed to the right.

cards.info: Under what specific condition will the IQR change when an outlier is added?
cards.backInfo: The IQR only changes if the outlier shifts the values of the 25th or 75th percentiles ($Q1$ or $Q3$).
